name: player_keeptradecut_value as_of_month_day 02-29 clamps to the month's last day in a non-leap year (executed-result parity)
description: make_date RAISES rather than returning null on February 29 of a non-leap year -- `select make_date(2023,2,29)` is `date field value out of range: 2023-02-29` -- and that aborts the whole statement, so the inner LEAST clamp is load-bearing rather than defensive. This is the highest-severity case for the param, because an unclamped build does not return a wrong value, it fails the entire request. Requests 02-29 across a non-leap year (2023) and a leap year (2024), seeding observations around February 28/29. The leap year must resolve the February 29 observation (200); the non-leap year must clamp its boundary to 2023-02-28 and resolve that day's observation (300); and no error may be raised. Goes red against a build whose boundary is a bare make_date(<year>, 2, 29) with no inner LEAST: the 2023 row raises 22008 and the request never returns. Note the boundary is MIDNIGHT at the start of the anchor day, exactly as date_trunc('day', opening_day) is on the opening-day branch, so each year's qualifying observation is seeded at or before that instant rather than during the anchor day.
